Boil the **2 lb baking potatoes** until tender, about **25 minutes** (typical). 2. Place the **1½ cans chopped tomatoes** in a colander and sprinkle with **salt**. Allow to drain **10–15 minutes** to rid them of as much moisture as possible. 3. Peel the potatoes and force through a sieve. Mix in the **⅛ c. olive oil**, **salt**, and **pepper**. 4. Oil a round pizza tray. Spread the potato mixture over it. 5. Arrange on top the **10 oz. sliced mozzarella**. Scatter on top the **8 chopped fillet anchovies**. 6. Preheat the oven to **400°**. Arrange the drained **tomatoes** over the potatoes. Sprinkle with **oregano**. Drizzle over the top the **⅛ c. olive oil**. 7. Bake **20 minutes**. Serve with **chopped parsley**.

Combine in a saucepan **3 tablespoons cornstarch** and **1 cup cold water**. Bring to a boil. 2. Add **¾ cup sugar**, **1 cup blueberries**, and **2 tablespoons lemon juice**. Cook until thick, about **3–5 minutes** (typical). Cool. 3. Pour **5 cups fresh blueberries** into a **graham cracker crust**. 4. Pour the cooked blueberry mixture over the fresh blueberries. 5. Chill until set, about **2–4 hours** (typical).

Beat at high speed.View on Kaper# Whoopee Pies ## Ingredients - 6 tablespoons Crisco solid shortening - 1 cup sugar - 1 egg - 1 teaspoon vanilla - 1 cup milk - 5 tablespoons cocoa - 2 cups flour - 1¼ teaspoons soda - 1 teaspoon salt ### Filling - ⅔ cup Crisco shortening - ½ cup granulated sugar - 1 tablespoon water - 1 teaspoon vanilla - ½ cup evaporated milk ## Directions 1. Cream the **6 tablespoons Crisco solid shortening**, **1 cup sugar**, and **1 egg**. 2. Add the **1 teaspoon vanilla** and **1 cup milk**. 3. Add the **5 tablespoons cocoa**, **2 cups flour**, **1¼ teaspoons soda**, and **1 teaspoon salt**. 4. Drop by tablespoon onto an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at **350°** for **10 minutes**. Cool. 5. Filling: combine in a mixing bowl the **⅔ cup Crisco shortening**, **½ cup granulated sugar**, **1 tablespoon water**, **1 teaspoon vanilla**, and **½ cup evaporated milk**. Beat at high speed for **10 minutes**. 6. Spread filling between two cookies.

scripts/readme.html.title: README
scripts/readme.html.description:
Rebuilds Obsidian recipe notes from FastFoto scans using macOS Vision OCR and USDA nutrition.Originals in FastFoto/1980s_reciepes and FastFoto/1990s_reciepes are never modified. Upright copies go to FastFoto/rotated/{era}/ and are embedded in each note.Duplex rotation (portrait FastFoto scans of landscape index cards): _a front = 90° clockwise, _b back = 270° clockwise (90° CCW / front + 180). Same long-edge flip as a typical ADF duplex scan. Pair/rotate/rebuild use this rule; do not reuse per-image OCR rotation for the display JPEGs.cd /Users/mattwatier/Repo/Recipe
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r Scripts/requirements.txt
xcrun swiftc -O -o Scripts/bin/ocr_vision Scripts/ocr_vision.swift \ -framework Vision -framework AppKit -framework Foundation
Put USDA_API_KEY= in Scripts/.env (gitignored). Never commit that file or paste the key into notes/README.Unprocessed notes live in Recipes/_Inbox/ as RAW OCR + source card images only (tiny YAML with kaper + card_id). Meal folders (Breakfast, Mains, Sides, Desserts, Drinks, Condiments) are for after processing. Mains have a major protein; Sides are vegetables, starches, and small-bite snacks.
Edit the RAW OCR in _Inbox against the card photos.
Move a note into Recipes/_Outbox/ when you want it turned into a recipe.
Run:
python Scripts/process_outbox.py
The processor:
reads RAW OCR from the note (plain text or markdown; sidecar only if that section is missing; does not re-OCR)
reconstructs a full recipe (Scripts/reconstruct.py): # / ## / **Serves:** are headings/metadata; ingredients inside directions are pulled out only if that food is not already listed (loose name match; prefer the Ingredients-section entry; keep the richer amount); a verb line plus a following list is one step; all stated bake/simmer/sauté times are summed into duration ({n}m); steps with no time get a typical duration. Clock times stay out of the step note. Overnight is never invented unless the card says so. Kaper YAML has no markdown; step titles are short actions and notes are instruction sentences
writes a Kaper fenced block plus cooking frontmatter (type, course, era from card_id, servings, times, oven, allergens)
estimates calories and macros per serving via the USDA API
leaves RAW OCR and image embeds intact
renames the file to the card’s recipe title when OCR has a clear title
files the finished note into the matching meal folder. Mains have a major protein; Sides are vegetables, starches, and small-bite snacks. Breakfast, drinks, desserts, and condiments stay their own folders.
Empty outbox is a no-op. Idempotent: a second run with nothing in _Outbox does nothing.Leave RAW OCR untouched. Markdown # / ## / **Serves:** are headings, not ingredients. Pull ingredients out of instructions; reconstruct card shorthand. Only add a direction-derived ingredient if that food is not already in the ingredient list. Match loosely on the food name (ignore amount, unit, prep note, and minor OCR spelling). Prefer the Ingredients-section entry; if one mention is quantified and the other is not, keep the richer amount. Sum all stated step times into duration ({n}m); infer typical times when missing. Clock times do not stay in the step note. Overnight is never invented unless the card says so.Kaper YAML cannot contain markdown. Strip **, #, _, backticks, and list markers from titles, notes, ingredient names, and tags. Leave markdown in ## RAW OCR.Kaper steps: title is a short action, optionally numbered (1. Steam, 2. Poach, 3. Combine & Garnish). note is a full instruction sentence. Clock times go in duration only. Keep qualitative doneness in the note (until tender, till fragrant, reduce by half). Optional tip: for extras such as internal temperature. Do not repeat whole-ingredient amounts in the instruction (Steam broccoli, not Steam 2 heads of broccoli); keep amounts only when subdividing. Cooking tools (dutch oven, buttered pan, mixing bowl) stay in the instruction, never the ingredient list. Encoding: Scripts/parse.py, Scripts/reconstruct.py (shape_step), Scripts/notes.emit_kaper. Reshape existing notes with python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --cleanup-steps.Kaper amount: is a whole number or decimal only — never a fraction. Unicode and ASCII fractions in RAW OCR (½ ¼ ¾ ⅓ ⅔ ⅛ 1/2 1/4 3/4, mixed 1½, fraction-slash 1⁄2) must become floats in YAML (amount: 0.5 or .5). The fraction glyph must not remain in name (including a leading ⁄2 after 1 was parsed separately).Kaper unit: is not part of name. Size words, kitchen measures, and weights all count. Recognize OCR aliases, then canonicalize:
Size / count: small, medium, large, whole, clove, can, stick
Volume: cups / c. → cup; tsp / t. / t → tsp; Tb / T. / T / tbsp / tablespoon → tbsp; pint → pt; quart → qt; pinch, dash, pkg
Weight: lbs / lb / pounds / # → lb; grams / g / gms → g; oz / ounces → oz
A # after an amount is pounds (2# beef → unit: lb), not a markdown heading.Kaper prep/knife directions belong in note, not in name. Match case-insensitively, including OCR near-misses. Canonical vocabulary: halve, quarter, wedge, chunk, rough chop, chop, fine chop, large dice, medium dice, small dice, mince, slice, thin slice, rings, strips, julienne, chiffonade, crush, smash, mince to a paste.Example — OCR ½ small onion, peeled and chopped → amount: 0.5, unit: small, name: onion, note: peeled and chopped. Wrong: amount: 1, name: ⁄2 small onion. Example — OCR 2 cloves garlic, minced → amount: 2, unit: clove, name: garlic, note: minced. Amount/unit/note parsing lives in Scripts/parse.py (parse_amount, split_amount_unit_name, UNIT_ALIASES, _split_note).Do not duplicate ingredients pulled from directions. If onion is already under Ingredients, do not add it again from "sauté the onion". Match loosely on food name (ignore amount/unit/prep and minor OCR spelling). Prefer the Ingredients-section entry; keep the richer amount if only one mention is quantified (Scripts/parse.py: food_names_match, dedupe_ingredients, add_new_ingredients).source .venv/bin/activate
